At the Africa Investment Forum’s Mission 300 Day in Rabat for a new-era partnerships, stronger national delivery capacity, and smart financing architectures.

The success of Africa’s energy transformation will not be measured by kilometres of cable laid, but by households switching on lights, health centres powering lifesaving equipment, and businesses growing with reliable, affordable electricity. Africa’s infrastructure is expanding fast—yet millions of connected households remain in the dark. Not only because the grid never reached them, but because they cannot afford to use it. 220 million Africans cannot afford basic electricity consumption, and 400 million cannot afford 500 kWh/year, barely a tenth of an average European household.

This affordability gap is one of the defining challenges for Africa’s economic future—but also a real opportunity to shape a new energy paradigm: one where investments are targeted, financing costs fall, and partnerships drive scalable, country-led solutions.

At the Africa Investment Forum’s Mission 300 Day in Rabat, I reaffirmed UNDP’s commitment to universal electrification in line with the UN-Energy Pledge. I had the pleasure to reflect with Aboubacar Said Anli, Minister of Energy, Water, and Hydrocarbons, #Comoros, Nialé Kaba, Minister of Minister of Planning and Development, #Côte d’Ivoire, Michael Franz , Team Leader, GET. Invest and moderated by Daniel Schroth Director at African Development Bank Group , on how to ensure electricity is not only available but affordable, inclusive, and transformative:

1️⃣ Shift from counting connections to measuring development outcomes — in health, education, livelihoods, and productivity.
2️⃣ Reduce the cost of capital, which is 3–4 times higher in Africa; narrowing this gap can cut project costs by 15–25%.
3️⃣ Strengthen partnerships across governments, DFIs, development partners, and the private sector to align financing and delivery at scale.

This is where Mission 300 becomes catalytic. With coordinated compacts, unified delivery frameworks, and blended investment pipelines, #M300 shows how strategic partnerships can amplify impact, accelerate financing, and translate ambition into real improvements in people’s lives. UNDP stands with the The World Bank , AfDB, and all Mission 300 partners in transforming energy systems into engines of development, inclusion, and resilience.
Kevin KARIUKI The Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet
